title: The Hubble tension: early versus late universe expansion
bottleneck: The cosmic microwave background implies a Hubble constant near 67 km/s/Mpc while local distance ladders measure about 73, a discrepancy now exceeding five sigma that has survived years of scrutiny on both sides. No single systematic error has been found, yet no new-physics model explains all the data cleanly.
why_it_blocks: A five-sigma crack in the standard cosmological model either reveals new physics or exposes unknown systematics in precision cosmology's flagship measurements; either way the model is incomplete.
current_state: Early dark energy, modified recombination, and interacting dark sector models can ease the tension but tend to worsen fits elsewhere, leaving the field without a compelling resolution. Gravitational-wave standard sirens offer a completely independent distance ladder that could break the deadlock within the next decade.
